candidates.name: Punta della Dogana
candidates.hours: Wed-Mon 10:00 to 19:00, closed Tue and Dec 24
candidates.content: Former customs house, centre for contemporary art, permanent exhibition of works from the François Pinault Collection. Renovation by world renowned architect Tadao Ando.

candidates.name: Gallerie dell'Accademia
candidates.hours: Mon 08:15-14:00, Tue-Sun 08:15-19:15 (ticket office closes 1 hr before)
candidates.content: Venice's most significant art museum which is also one of Italy's best. Among the most important paintings in the Accademia are: Gentile Bellini: Procession on St. Mark’s Square (1496) and Miracle of the Cross at the Bridge of S.

candidates.name: The Peggy Guggenheim Museum
candidates.price: Adult €17, seniors (over 65 years) €15, students (25 years and under with valid student ID) €10, youth 10-18 €9, 9 and younger free
candidates.hours: Wed-Mon 10:00-18:00. Closed on Tuesdays and on 25 December. Open on national holidays (including Tuesdays)
candidates.content: Offers a personal collection of modern art collected by Peggy Guggenheim. Peggy was an American married to modern artist Max Ernst, and funded a number of his contemporaries. The gallery includes a sculpture garden and works by Pi

candidates.name: Doge's Palace
candidates.hours: Nov to Mar 08:30 to 17:30, Apr to Oct 08:30 to 19:00, closed Jan 1 and Dec 25
candidates.content: Don't miss the guided tour named Secret Itinerary, which will let you discover the part of the palace where the city's administration worked, as well as Casanova's jail and the wonderful five hundred year old roof structure. A MUV

candidates.name: Clock tower
candidates.content: Having been closed for restoration for many years, the restored astronomical clock is now visible. The fascinating tour of the clock mechanism (and rooftop bell) can only be visited on a guided tour, in English: M-W at 10:00 and 1

candidates.name: Saint Mark's Basilica
candidates.price: Admission to the basilica is free, however, the museum upstairs costs €5 and to view the high altar and treasury costs €2 and €3 respectively
candidates.content: Saint Mark's Basilica is on the Piazza San Marco and is one of the highlights of a visit to Venice. As with most churches in Italy, you must be dressed appropriately to be allowed in; this means no short skirts or bare shoulders.

candidates.name: Correr Museum
candidates.hours: Nov 1 to Mar 31: 10:00-17:00, Apr 1 to Oct 31: 10:00-19:00, closed Dec 25, Jan 1
candidates.content: Interesting collection of globes, starting from the 16th century. There is also an only library hall, an archeological museum of Roman antiques and an important picture gallery. The museum offers a tour of Venetian history. Remark

candidates.name: Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari
candidates.alt: Basilica dei Frai, often just referred to as the Frari
candidates.hours: Mon-Fri 09:00-18:00, Sun and holidays 13:00-18:00. Last admission 30 min before closing time
candidates.content: The big friary church, fine example of Venetian Gothic architecture, with fine monuments and paintings of Titian, Belliniand Donatello, among which the famous 'Assunta' by Titian.

candidates.name: Ca' Pesaro - Museum of Oriental Art
candidates.alt: Museo d'arte Orientale di Ca Pesaro
candidates.price: Adults €14, reduced €11.50 (valid for both museums in the Ca' Pesaro)
candidates.hours: Nov-Mar 10:00 to 17:00, Apr-Oct: 10 :00-18:00, closed Mon, Dec 25, Jan 1, May 1
candidates.content: Beautiful palace housing the gallery of modern art focusing on Italian art in the 19th century as well as the Marco Polo Museum, a rich collection mainly of Asian exhibits (fabrics, clothes, armours, porcelain). A MUVE museum.

candidates.name: Jewish Museum
candidates.price: Entrance: adults €3, reduced €2. Entrance with guided tours to synagogues: adults €8.50, reduced €7
candidates.hours: 1 Jun-30 Sep: 10:00-19:00; 1 Oct-31 May: 10:00-18:00. Closed on Sat (Shabbat), during Jewish festivities, on 25 Dec, 1 Jan and 1 May
candidates.content: Objects related to the social life of the Jewish community, in two synagogues of the 16th century.

candidates.name: Santa Maria di Nazareth Church
candidates.alt: Chiesa di Santa Maria di Nazareth
candidates.content: Also known as Church of the Scalzi (Chiesa degli Scalzi), being the seat in the city of the Discalced Carmelites religious order (scalzi in Italian means "barefoot"). Built in the mid 17th century to the designs of Baldassarre Lon

candidates.name: San Michele Cemetery
candidates.content: Cemetery established following Napoleon Bonaparte's edict of 1804, part of the European circuit of monumental cemeteries. The Russian ballet director Sergei Diaghilev, the Austrian physicist Christan Doppler, the American poet Ezr

candidates.name: Bridge of Sighs
candidates.content: Connecting the Doge's Palace with the prison. Persons convicted in the palace were passing to prison here, seeing the last of Venice before going into the dark prison area with no daylight. You can pass the bridge yourself during

candidates.name: San Giovanni e Paolo
candidates.content: A fine, huge Dominican church with the tombs of many Doges. It shares its piazza with the fine Renaissance façade of the Scuola San Marco and an equestrian statue of the mercenary captain Bartolomeo Colleoni (see below).

candidates.name: Santa Maria della Pietà
candidates.content: A church that used to house an orphanage and hospital in the 18th century, it is known among classical music enthusiasts as the church where the Catholic priest and composer Antonio Vivaldi worked for most of his career.

candidates.name: S. Maria Formosa
candidates.content: The first church dedicated to "Mary of the Forms" was built on this spot in the VII century, when the Virgin ordered bishop Magnus to erect one, appearing to him as an exceedingly shapely woman. The current building, planned by Co

candidates.name: Museo Diocesano
candidates.content: Religious furniture and objects from now demolished churches and convents, one of the most appealing Romanesque cloisters of Venice.

candidates.name: Scuola Dalmatina di San Giorgio e Trifone
candidates.content: Famous painting cycle by Vittore Carpaccio depicting the lives of St.George, Tryphon and Jerome.

candidates.name: Equestrian statue of Bartolomeo Colleoni
candidates.content: The famous condottiere (1395–1475) had a long and remunerative career as captain of a mercenary army fighting for (or against, depending on the pay) the Republic, but died without an heir (8 daughters did not count) and bequeathed

candidates.name: I Gesuati
candidates.content: 18th-century Dominican church on the Giudecca canal. The classical style building has a well-lit interior and is exceptional in preserving its original layout and Rococo decoration intact. The church and almost all its sculpture a

candidates.name: S. Maria della Salute
candidates.content: As a votive offering for the city's deliverance from the Black Plague, the church was designed in the then fashionable Baroque style. Construction began in 1631. Most of the objects of art housed in the church bear references to t

candidates.name: Church of Saint Sebastian
candidates.content: 16th-century Roman Catholic church, houses a cycle of paintings by the artist Paolo Veronese as well as paintings by Tintoretto and Titian. Includes the tomb of Paolo Veronese, a painter from Verona whose career was in Venice (152

candidates.name: Gallery Palazzo Cini
candidates.content: Former residence of Italian industrialist Vittorio Cini who amassed large collection of Italian art. The gallery houses a collection of 15th and 16th cent paintings from Tuscany and Ferrara, period furniture, silver, ivory and cer

candidates.name: Scuola Grande dei Carmini
candidates.content: Painting cycles dedicated to the Madonna del Carmine, canvases by Tiepolo and Padoviano.

candidates.name: Monastery of San Nicolò al Lido
candidates.content: Monastery and church that houses some relics of Saint Nicholas (270–343 AD), patron of sailors. Both the church and monastery dates back to the 16th century.

candidates.name: Basilica San Giorgio Maggiore
candidates.price: For the bell tower: €6, reduced rate €4 (students and 65+)
candidates.content: Designed by Andrea Palladio and build 1566-1610. Very nice views of Venice from the bell tower.

candidates.name: Palazzo Grassi
candidates.hours: Mon Wed-Sun 10:00-19:00. Last admission 1 hr before closing
candidates.content: Contemporary art museum. Temporary exhibitions from François Pinault's Collection.

candidates.name: Palazzo Fortuny
candidates.content: Collection of paintings and lamps. A MUVE museum.

candidates.name: Teatro Malibran
candidates.content: Teatro Malibran was built in 1678, and is now part of La Fenice. Tickets for opera, ballet, and symphony performances are available at La Fenice, various locations around the city, or by phone .

candidates.name: La Fenice Theatre
candidates.price: Tours: adults €10, students up to 26 and seniors over 65 €7, children up to 6 free. Slightly cheaper if purchased as part of a combined ticket with the Doge's palace. Performances €10-380
candidates.content: One of the best opera houses in the world. The theatre is an identical reconstruction (rebuilt in 2003) of the previous theatre building that burned down in 1996. Tickets for opera, ballet, and symphony performances are available

candidates.name: Venice Casino
candidates.price: Entrance €10, free if you are booked at selected hotels
candidates.content: The oldest gambling house in the world, founded in 1638. The building dates back to the 15th century.

candidates.name: Ateneo San Basso
candidates.content: Classical concerts.

candidates.name: Chiesa San Vidal
candidates.content: Classical concerts by Interpreti Veneziani. They also run the nearby Music Museum in the nearby San Maurizio church.

candidates.name: Teatro San Gallo
candidates.content: Half-hour documentary based on the BBC series Francesco's Venice - an 'amazing film that puts the spectacular beauty of this great city in historical context'. Film in English, audioguides in Italian, Russian and Spanish.

candidates.name: The Avogaria Theatre
candidates.content: The smallest theatre in Venice, housed in an unassuming former workshop.

candidates.name: Chiesa della Pietà
candidates.content: Between 1703 and 1740, Antonio Vivaldi taught the orchestra of the girls in the orphanage here, writing unparalleled music for them. Frequent concerts of his Four Seasons by a Baroque ensemble.

candidates.name: Orsoni Furnace
candidates.content: One of the last industries left in Venice, the Orsoni Furnace produces fine glass panels and mosaics using the same technique since 1888. The small factory can only be visited on certain dates.

candidates.name: Northern Giudecca canal walk
candidates.content: It's a long and sunny walk along the Giudecca canal, protected during winter time from cold northerly winds for being exposed to south and shielded by buildings. You might find interesting to see how a gondola is made, stopping by

candidates.name: Squero di San Trovaso
candidates.content: Squero is Venetian for small ship yard.

candidates.name: Venice International Film Festival
candidates.content: Attend the annual film festival, the oldest of its kind. It is organized by La Biennale di Venezia and usually takes place around late August or early September. Make your reservations early as the island is small and hotels fill

candidates.name: Scuola Grande di S.Teodoro
candidates.content: Opera and concert performances.

candidates.name: Southern Giudecca canal walk
candidates.content: Like the northern version you walk along the entire Giudecca canal, but in this case on the Giudecca island.

candidates.name: Oasi Dune degli Alberoni
candidates.content: Visit the natural oasis in Alberoni, a WWF protected area of about 1.6 km² at the southern tip of the Lido.

candidates.name: Energy Darshan
candidates.content: A center for meditation and relaxation.

candidates.name: Harry's Bar-Ristorante
candidates.content: The Bellini-cocktail was invented here. Ernest Hemingway was one of the most famous guests. Very pricy!

candidates.name: Cantine del Vino gia Schiavi
candidates.content: Inventive and delicious cicchetti; pile a plate with what you like, and the staff will pour you a glass of wine to match the selection. If it's too crowded inside, step out and find a space by the canal. A large and carefully cura

candidates.name: Caffè Florian
candidates.content: On the extravagant side there is Caffè Florian, on Piazza San Marco. It claims to be the oldest coffee house still in operation, established in 1720. The interior is about a century newer, and brings an exclusive setting for a cup

candidates.name: Al Parlamento
candidates.content: Another small bar, away from the main tourist arteries. Serves spritz, cocktails and beer with a view of the Cannaregio canal.

candidates.name: Pub Taverna L'Olandese Volante
candidates.content: Located between the Rialto Bridge and Piazza San Marco. During the summertime there are tables outside when you can easily sit and rest after a day of wandering around this marvelous city. What is more, during the day pasta and ot

candidates.name: Caffe Quadri
candidates.content: Opposite Caffè Florian, with similar prices.

candidates.name: La Bottiglia
candidates.content: A small wine bar with excellent reviews. They offer a small but constantly changing selection of wines, complemented by excellent Italian street food and snacks.

candidates.name: Osteria da Filo
candidates.content: An excellent place to fill up on some aperitifs and meet the local student crowd. Aperol Spritz is €2.50, a bargain for being in central Venice. The bar also hosts live music from time to time.

candidates.name: Bacareto da Lele
candidates.content: A Venetian institution that's been around since 1968. This minuscule bar serves cheap wine, a small glass is just one euro, and excellent cichetti to go along. Queuing is the norm, but the bartenders are very quick and you'll be s

candidates.name: E Rosa Salva
candidates.content: One of the favorites is the mini-chain "E Rosa Salva", with three locations in the center - on C. Fiubera (from Piazza San Marco, take the underpass in the middle of the arcade, cross the bridge and take second right off C. Fabbri

candidates.name: Vino Vero
candidates.content: Small wine bar with excellent selection, away from the tourist crowds. Outdoor seating next to one of the canals.

candidates.name: Chet Bar
candidates.content: The closest thing to a dive bar you'll find in Venice, except that the cocktails actually are pretty good.

candidates.name: Devils Forest Pub
candidates.content: A traditional English style pub with a very fun atmosphere. It is located near the Rialto Bridge and tucked into a small alley near the Disney Store.

candidates.name: Al Vecio Canton
candidates.content: This small and atmospheric restaurant/pizzeria will absolutely enchant you. Famous for its traditional style pizza and seafood pasta, you will not only get it all at affordable prices (pizza from €7.50, pasta from €10, wine from €

candidates.name: Al Timon
candidates.content: Warm and local atmosphere in this little osteria where they serve great Italian vintages by the glass. If you're adventurous, try their tasty tripe. Good music inside, some table by the canal in the summer. Reservations on evening

candidates.name: Pizza al volo
candidates.content: Sells superb pizza by the (extremely large) slice in Campo Santa Margherita for approximately €1.80 a slice, €5 a whole pizza. It is by the fresh fish stall under a green awning.

candidates.name: La Bitta
candidates.content: This busy but friendly restaurant is in the more studenty area of Dorsoduro, and attracts a mixture of locals and tourists. They have some excellent Italian dishes, which are reflected in the prices, plus they have a great selecti

candidates.name: Trattoria Andri
candidates.content: Serves local Venetian seafood delicacies such as squid in ink over polenta (not as bad as it sounds), shrimp scampi and octopus, among other more common dishes. Water is served in Murano glass vases. Inside, pictures of celebritie

candidates.name: Trattoria Busa alla Torre Da Lele
candidates.content: A typical trattoria, frequented by both tourists and locals. Excellent food.

candidates.name: Restaurant La Caravella
candidates.hours: Open every day all year round
candidates.content: Historical place near St. Mark's Square, known since the 1960s, it has become a must if you like traditions. Offers some typical dishes and a large selection of wines. From May to September service is in a traditional courtyard.

candidates.name: Antico Dolo
candidates.content: An old seafood restaurant close to Rialto bridge: food comes from the adjacent Rialto Market daily. A complete dinner excluding wines could cost €35 each more or less.

candidates.name: Osteria Mocenigo
candidates.content: Little restaurant frequented by locals. Be sure to try their antipasti. Excellent desserts too.

candidates.name: Crepes House by PePe
candidates.content: Savory and sweet crepes

candidates.name: Rialto Market
candidates.content: This vegetable and fish market has been running for hundreds of years, an essential stop for home cooks in central Venice.

december.text: If you'd rather avoid the highway traffic and don't have bulky luggage, take the local Mobilita di Marca bus no. 6 for €1.30 (€2.50 if bought on board). It will deposit you at the Treviso train station in about 10 minutes. There are 2-3 departures hourly from the airport between 06:00 to 22:00. Then it's about 30 minut

Venice is well-connected with the domestic train network, Rome and Milan are only a few hours away. Freccia Bianca (White Arrow) trains to Trieste leave from Venezia Mestre several times a day and the trip takes about 1 hr 35 min. Regionale Veloce (Fast Regional) trains leave from Santa Lucia station frequently, the tr

Trains from the mainland run through Mestre on the mainland to the terminus Venezia Santa Lucia railway station on the west side of Venice; make sure you don't get it confused with the two stations on the mainland before the bridge. Many through trains only stop in Mestre, in that case just hop on to one of the very fr

While Venice may not get more tourists than other famous Italian destinations such as Rome and Florence, the narrowness of streets and open areas may at times make Venice feel uncomfortably crowded during (but not only) the peak seasons, at the San Marco sestiere, the surroundings of the Rialto bridge and the streets l

Cannaregio is one six sestieri (districts) that make up Venice. For many travellers, it's the first part of Venice they enter, since Venezia Santa Lucia railway station, the main railway station, is here. Most of the district is residential, with slightly less tourists - and sights - compared to other parts of the city

Monastery of San Nicolò al Lido: Monastery and church that houses some relics of Saint Nicholas (270–343 AD), patron of sailors. Both the church and monastery dates back to the 16th century.

Arrival to Santa Croce is straightforward, it's the district that most travelers will arrive into if travelling by bus, car or tram.
